A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RPS research work. The main text, figures, algorithms, equations, and complete appendices are readable, and retained material can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: Section 7 and the appendices report original image-classification experiments measuring certified reliability, coverage, prediction-set sizes, computational costs, and ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains the original experiments and adds CIFAR100 results, partition-count sensitivity results, and a repeated empirical-coverage study.

M1.justification: The changed alpha_n formula in Theorem 1 revises the stated calibration rule used by Algorithm 2. Hash partitioning, classifier training, smoothed voting, majority aggregation, and certification algorithms otherwise remain intact. The PDFs do not establish an implementation change or rerun.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate image classification on SVHN, CIFAR10, and CIFAR100. CIFAR100 and the calibration-poisoning setting already appear in v1; the added plots and coverage study extend measurements within retained dataset and task coverage.

E2.justification: New Figure 13 explicitly compares majority prediction sets against full-calibration HPS and unmerged per-partition HPS, labeled 'Smaller HPS.' This adds comparison controls for the concentration analysis. Existing softmax and APS comparisons are retained.

E3.justification: Figure 10 introduces AUCRC, the area under the certifiable reliability curve. Appendix C adds a full-versus-partitioned calibration design using ResNet18 on CIFAR10, nominal coverage 0.9, and 10 or 20 partitions. Existing training settings and the stated 1,000/9,000 calibration/test split are unchanged.

E4.justification: Figure 10 adds sensitivity analysis of certified reliability to calibration-partition count across three datasets. Appendix C and Figure 13 test whether majority aggregation restores coverage concentration lost through partitioning. Existing softmax, architecture, poisoning-radius, and reproducibility analyses remain.

E5.justification: Both versions retain five classifier initializations, five calibration splits per classifier, and mean/standard-deviation reporting. New Appendix C specifies 100 repetitions and displays coverage distributions as violin plots. This is a separate repeated-run study, not a stated increase in repetitions for the earlier experiments.

E6.justification: Figures 9, 10, and 13 add CIFAR100 results, generally increasing AUCRC with more partitions, and coverage distributions showing majority sets more concentrated than per-partition HPS. Section 7 changes 'five classifiers suffice' to four. Existing headline results, including 92.3% coverage and average size 3.6 for joint poisoning, are retained.

T1.justification: Theorem 1 replaces ceil((n+1)(1-alpha))/n with floor(alpha(n+1)-1); Proposition 1's derivation changes accordingly while retaining its minimum-size bound. Theorem 6 replaces tau with the majority threshold tau-hat(alpha). These are localized mathematical revisions, although v2 leaves the quantile-level versus integer-index convention unclear.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: efficient RPS construction, reliability certificates against training and calibration poisoning, and empirical utility. Explicit insertion/deletion wording in the introduction describes the threat model already defined in v1.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the new coverage distributions as evidence of statistical efficiency, explicitly distinguishes marginal coverage from pointwise reliability, and explains how calibration-aware training attacks can undermine exchangeability. Desideratum IV is qualified as algorithmic flexibility to improve reliability with more data. Existing large-dataset accuracy limitations remain.

D1.justification: Appendix A retains the same optimizer hyperparameters, training budget, preprocessing, deterministic-training instructions, hardware, and runtime information. Both versions promise future release of source code and random seeds; access information is unchanged.

R1.justification: The bibliography is unchanged, but Section 2 sharpens the distinction between pointwise reliability and prior conformal-coverage guarantees. It specifically states that Zargarbashi et al. (2024) addresses calibration-data modifications without supporting adversarial insertion or deletion.

P1.justification: Localized rewrites clarify the background, desiderata, majority threshold, and discussion, including a main-text proof sketch. A new statistical-efficiency appendix is inserted, shifting existing Appendices C–E to D–F. The main section sequence and overall narrative remain.

P2.justification: v2 adds Figures 9, 10, and 13 and reflows the appendices. The earlier Figures 9–11 are retained as Figures 11, 12, and 14. Existing plots and the main document's visual style are preserved.

improvement.justification: The added partition-sensitivity and 100-repeat coverage analyses provide useful evidence about reliability and calibration variability, while clearer distinctions between marginal coverage and pointwise reliability improve interpretation. These are limited gains with the headline results retained. The revised alpha_n formula still leaves quantile normalization unclear, so the mathematical edits cannot be treated as a complete repair.
